questions.stem: A man walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south. How far is he from the starting point, and in what direction?
questions.explanation: Start at origin. +5 km N to (0,5). +3 km E to (3,5). +5 km S to (3,0). Final displacement = 3 km east of starting point. The two 5-km legs cancel; only the 3-km east leg survives. 13 km is the total distance walked, not displacement.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: A cyclist rides 4 km east, then 3 km north. How far is she from the start in a straight line?
questions.explanation: Straight-line (shortest) distance = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 km. 7 km is the sum of the two legs (total distance walked, not displacement). 3-4-5 is the classic Pythagorean triple — worth memorising for speed.

questions.stem: If south-east becomes north, north-east becomes west, and so on, what will west become?
questions.explanation: The directions are being rotated 135° anticlockwise (SE = 135° → N = 0°). Applying the same rotation to W (270°): 270° − 135° = 135° → SE. Method: work out the rotation from the first pair, apply the same to the asked direction. Anticlockwise: SE → N → NW → W → SW → S → SE → ...

questions.stem: A man starts from point A and walks 10 m east, then turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right again and walks 10 m. How far is he from A and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Start at A (0,0). 10 m east → (10,0). Turn right (now facing south) + 5 m → (10,−5). Turn right again (now facing west) + 10 m → (0,−5). Final position 5 m south of A. Right turns when walking east: next is south, then west, then north.

questions.stem: Raj walks 6 km north, then 8 km west, then 6 km south. His displacement from the starting point is:
questions.explanation: Start at (0,0). +6 N → (0,6). −8 E (i.e., 8 km west) → (−8,6). −6 N (6 km south) → (−8,0). Displacement = 8 km west. The 6-km north and 6-km south cancel. 20 km is the total path length (6+8+6).

questions.stem: A boy facing north turns 90° clockwise, then 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Measure rotations clockwise from north as positive. Net rotation = +90° − 135° = −45°, i.e., 45° anticlockwise from north = North-West. Verification step-by-step: start facing N, +90° CW puts him facing E, then −135° CCW moves him back by 135° (E → N → NW), landing on NW.

questions.stem: From town P, Q is 30 km east. R is 40 km north of Q. The shortest distance from P to R is:
questions.explanation: P is at (0,0); Q at (30,0); R at (30,40). PR = √(30² + 40²) = √(900 + 1600) = √2500 = 50 km. 70 km is 30 + 40, the total path via Q. Another Pythagorean triple worth memorising — 3-4-5 scaled up ten times.
